viewer_question: How did the Black Death travel across distant medieval towns?
promise: Follow the epidemic through connected trade routes and ports.
title: How the Black Death Spread Across Medieval Europe
thumbnail_situation: A medieval cargo ship enters a crowded port while dockworkers unload goods; the hand-drawn traveler watches from the quay. No visible disease, no Tower Bridge, no coins.
visual_hierarchy: Incoming ship first, wary port crowd second, traveler as a small recurring guide.

viewer_question: What did ordinary people do when someone near them became sick?
promise: See the personal choices around care, closeness and distance during the plague.
title: The Black Death: How Medieval People Faced the Plague
thumbnail_situation: Inside a 14th-century home, a caregiver sets a bowl by a sick family member; the drawn traveler observes quietly from the threshold. Respectful, no gore, no death tableau.
visual_hierarchy: Caregiver and bowl dominate; sick person is clearly alive; traveler is secondary.

viewer_question: How did mass death change bargaining over work and wages?
promise: Follow labor shortages, worker bargaining and attempts by authorities to control wages.
title: How the Black Death Changed Work and Wages in Europe
thumbnail_situation: A field worker and landholder face each other in a tense wage negotiation, with an official holding a posted ordinance; the drawn traveler watches from the middle distance. No legible secondary text.
visual_hierarchy: Worker's firm gesture and landholder's open wage pouch dominate; traveler is secondary.
